solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Temperance group's anti-drugs slogan receiving opprobrium from home at first

indicators.note: the slogan takes the other letters into itself, like a person receiving guests

parts.note: a two-word rallying cry against drugs: ban dope

indicators.note: the opening letters of the three words before it are taken

explanation.surface: A temperance society's anti-drug slogan is met with scorn from people at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes the opening letters of 'opprobrium from home', which 'receiving' places inside the slogan BAN DOPE, just after its D.
explanation.definitionFit: This Victorian movement, founded in 1847 in Leeds, signed children up to lifelong abstinence from alcohol, so it is a temperance organisation.

clue.text: White and black side of red rose trimmed

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: trimmed means the word loses its tail end

parts.note: the red rose is Lancashire's emblem, and its county cricket side is Lancs for short

explanation.surface: A rose-grower describing the colours of a Lancashire bloom with its petals cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: The red rose is the emblem of Lancashire, an English county; its cricket side is Lancs. 'trimmed' cuts off the S, leaving LANC.
explanation.definitionFit: French for white, used in English for white wine such as sauvignon blanc.

clue.text: Part of insect's leg raised on stomach

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so leg can mean on
tum is the informal word for stomach

explanation.surface: An entomologist notes that an insect's leg is lifted up on its belly.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also the on side; 'raised' reads that upwards. The 'on' after it is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Entomologists use this name for the upper, back-facing plate of an insect's thorax segment.

clue.text: Cycling event team hug, right after swimming medley

parts.note: the omnium is a multi-race track cycling event

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters moving about and becoming rearranged

explanation.surface: Cyclists share a team hug after a swimming medley relay, as in a triathlon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medley' looks like part of the swimming picture but is the definition. 'after' only says where R stands among the letters 'swimming' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumble or miscellaneous collection of things, which is what a medley is.

clue.text: Put on trial screening of women ignoring doctor finally turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
ignoring means a letter is left out of the word

parts.note: purdah is the custom of keeping women hidden from men or strangers

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word doctor

explanation.surface: Someone is charged over the screening of women, with the doctor's final turn-up ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops R, the end of 'doctor', from PURDAH to give PUDAH, and 'turning up' reads that upwards as HADUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hauled up before a court is informal British usage for being brought to trial.

clue.text: Artwork exercises family woman with delicate touch

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school exercises
nan is a grandmother, a woman in the family
a dink is a softly played shot, as in tennis

explanation.surface: An artwork shows a woman exercising with her family, painted with a delicate touch.
explanation.walkthrough: NAN is British for grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing done in a nib and black liquid is a kind of artwork, named after its materials.

clue.text: Diver heads for surface, making enormous waves

indicators.note: heads gives the front letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A diving bird comes up to the surface, causing huge waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads for' looks like 'goes towards', but it takes the first letters of the next four words.
explanation.definitionFit: This small sea duck feeds by diving underwater, so it is a diving bird.

clue.text: Chairman adding nothing in complex passages on the character of Lear

indicators.note: in places the zero inside the maze

parts.note: a maze is a network of complicated passages
O looks like zero, nothing
the Dong with a Luminous Nose is a character in a nonsense poem by Edward Lear

explanation.surface: A chairman adds nothing to complicated passages about King Lear's character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lear' suggests Shakespeare's king, but it is Edward Lear, whose nonsense poem features the Dong with a Luminous Nose. 'in' places the zero inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Chairman Mao led the Chinese Communist Party, and his title was Chairman.

clue.text: Long Rolls? They might include one

parts.note: to long for something is to wish for it
rolls are lists of names, as in electoral rolls

explanation.surface: A baker's question about long bread rolls and what they might contain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' and 'Rolls' look like bakery words but are a verb and a noun for lists. In the definition, 'one' stands for a wish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lists of wanted things each contain at least one wish, so they might include one.

clue.text: A duck flies — or a number

parts.note: a duck is a nought in cricket, and love is nought in tennis
something that flies is up aloft, in the sky

explanation.surface: A duck takes off, or perhaps a count of birds is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a zero score in cricket, and in tennis zero is called love.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a 1970s disco hit, and a song can be called a number.

clue.text: Receptive backing of French teachers who've organised volunteers

indicators.note: backing means the string of pieces runs backwards

parts.note: de is French for of
the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, teachers organised in a union
the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: French teachers backing a scheme for volunteers are open to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the whole string of three pieces round, not just one. The NUT was a British teachers' union and the TA is Britain's army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in harmony with, or sensitive to, other people's views is receptive to them.

clue.text: Son once travelling right across the US

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters moving around into a new order

explanation.surface: A son once journeyed right across America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right across the US' looks like a description of the trip, but it is the definition: right-wingers in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoconservatives are a right-wing political faction found in the United States.

clue.text: Approach step to receive new punishment?

parts.note: to come up is to approach

indicators.note: the step takes in the next letter, as if receiving it

parts.note: a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: Someone is told to step forward and receive a new punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting what one deserves, usually a fitting penalty, is a just punishment.

clue.text: Slipper, or part of one, hard to shift

indicators.note: to shift means the letter is moved away, taken out

parts.note: the heel is part of a slipper or shoe
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A slipper, or part of it, proves hard to remove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slipper' looks like footwear but is the definition: a slippery creature. 'one' refers back to the slipper.
explanation.definitionFit: This fish is notoriously slippery to hold, so it is something that slips.

clue.text: Possible argument with van Persie's beginning: Gunners no good!

indicators.note: beginning takes the opening letter of the footballer's surname

parts.note: the RA, Royal Artillery, are gunners

explanation.surface: A fan grumbles about Robin van Persie's start at Arsenal, the Gunners: no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van Persie' looks like one name, but 'van' belongs to the definition and only Persie's first letter is used. Arsenal FC are nicknamed the Gunners, but here it is the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor car crash in British slang, such as a bump with a van, may well lead to a row.

clue.text: Pity USSR has re-formed, imprisoning old dissident group

indicators.note: imprisoning means one piece is held inside the other
re-formed means the letters are formed again in another order

explanation.surface: A pity the USSR has come back, jailing an old group of dissidents.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-formed' rearranges PITYUSSR, and 'imprisoning' puts O inside it to give PUSSYRIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: This Russian feminist protest punk band had members jailed after a protest, so it is a group of dissidents.

clue.text: Drink with artist, saving kiss for princess

indicators.note: saving here means keeping safe inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: ale is a drink
and can mean with, as in fish and chips
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone drinking with an artist holds back a kiss meant for a princess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' looks like 'except', but it means holding: the kiss sits inside the drink-with-artist string. RA is a Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandra was the Danish-born wife of Edward VII, Princess of Wales before becoming queen.

clue.text: Squish flies with ounce weight for entertainment on box

indicators.note: flies suggests the letters scattering into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Squashing flies with an ounce weight, as if for a television entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' looks like insects but signals that SQUISH, OZ and W are rearranged together. 'box' is British slang for television.
explanation.definitionFit: Television programmes where contestants answer questions are popular entertainment on the box.

clue.text: Italy's players question Arsenal midfielder briefly: appeal overturned

indicators.note: briefly means the name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Mikel Arteta played in midfield for Arsenal

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: it means sex appeal, as in 'she's got it'

explanation.surface: A fan questions an Arsenal midfielder briefly after an appeal was overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italy's players' looks like a football team but means Italian musicians. Arteta played for Arsenal, a London club, around 2012.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Italian plural for groups of four musicians, so Italian players.

clue.text: Rabbit to get round dog — little time involved

indicators.note: involved means taken into the middle of the other word

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow or stalk them
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A rabbit tries to get round a dog, with little time to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' looks like an animal, but it is British rhyming slang for talk (rabbit and pork). 'involved' puts the little time inside the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattering talk used to win someone over is chatter meant to get round them.

clue.text: Retro paper cups for one hot drink

indicators.note: cups means holding inside, as hands cup something
retro, looking back, means the word runs backwards

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
for one means for example, which is eg

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned newspaper serves up one hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid. 'Retro' turns it round, and 'cups' wraps it round the abbreviation meaning for example.
explanation.definitionFit: This hot mixture of wine, water, sugar and spice was a traditional warming drink.

clue.text: Approval that ends on 30 September?

definitions.meaning: a vote in favour, an aye, is approval
a calendar ... stopped at the end of September has run only three of its four quarters, so the word for it loses its last quarter, its final letter

explanation.surface: A query about which approval scheme expires at the end of September.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part is a whimsical picture, not a dictionary sense: cut off at 30 September, a year is three quarters done, and so is the four-letter word for it, stopping before its R.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for yes, used in voting, so it expresses approval.

clue.text: Homer's treated with tasty offer from Bart

indicators.note: treated means the letters are processed and reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Homer Simpson is treated to something tasty offered by his son Bart.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Homer's' gives its S to the letters rearranged here, with TASTY.
explanation.definitionFit: This rude invitation is Bart Simpson's catchphrase, offered to anyone who annoys him.

clue.text: Year-old antelope being reared?

indicators.note: in a down clue, reared means lifted up, read from the bottom

parts.note: the gnu is an African antelope

explanation.surface: A one-year-old antelope is being brought up by its herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being reared' turns GNU upwards into UNG. The whole clue also describes offspring being brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring still being brought up by their parents are collectively their brood.

clue.text: Former Home Secretary having drunk his last gets carried out again

indicators.note: having drunk means taking something inside, as a drinker takes in liquid

parts.note: John Reid was British Home Secretary in 2006 and 2007
his refers to Reid, and his last letter is D

explanation.surface: A former Home Secretary, having had one drink too many, is carried out once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his last' is the final letter of REID itself, which 'having drunk' places inside the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing a task a second time is doing it again, so the past tense fits.

clue.text: Fool discounting odds, form, checks tips

indicators.note: tips means turns over, so the letters are reversed
discounting odds drops the first, third and fifth letters, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A punter ignores the odds and the form, relying instead on tips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discounting odds' keeps OM from 'form' and HCS from 'checks', and 'tips' turns OMHCS over. 'tips' looks like betting advice.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yiddish-derived American slang word for a stupid or contemptible person.

clue.text: Badly bound, it's far from fixed

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put together wrongly, out of order

parts.note: the apostrophe-s is a link here, so only the two letters of it go into the mix

explanation.surface: A poorly bound book is far from being repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'it's' is a link, so only IT goes into the rearranged letters with BOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncertain or undecided is far from settled.

clue.text: Hesitate, being from the East End: was forced to come west

indicators.note: East End Londoners, Cockneys, traditionally drop the aitch at the start of words

parts.note: a human is a being

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming west means reading right to left

parts.note: had, as in 'had to go', means was forced

explanation.surface: Someone from the East End of London, made to move west, hesitates.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the Cockney part of London, where H is dropped: HUMAN becomes UMAN. 'to come west' turns HAD into DAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'um' and 'ah' is dithering in speech, so it means to waver or hesitate.

clue.text: Small amphibian kicked out of one's trap

indicators.note: trap is slang for mouth, so words coming out of one's trap are spoken, said rather than written

parts.note: to toe something is to kick it with the toe, so kicked is toed

explanation.surface: A little frog-like creature gets booted out of the snare it was caught in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trap' looks like a snare, but it is slang for mouth (as in 'shut your trap'), so 'out of one's trap' says the word is spoken: TOED, said, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A warty, frog-like creature that lives on land and breeds in water is an amphibian.

clue.text: Was Spice Girl idle music-maker?

parts.note: did can stand in for was in a question: did ... do?
Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice in the Spice Girls
do 0, do nothing, means to be idle

explanation.surface: A question about whether one of the Spice Girls was lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the pieces as 'Did Geri do O?', did Geri do nothing, which asks whether she was idle; O stands for zero.
explanation.definitionFit: This long wooden Aboriginal Australian wind instrument produces a drone, so it makes music.
